stories.headline: 2026 MLB wild-card series Day 2: Live updates, lineups, analysis
stories.summary: Which teams will sweep and which will force a Game 3? We've got it all covered for you.
stories.body:
Who is ready for some more postseason baseball?

The Philadelphia Phillies started things off with yet another dramatic comeback win to even the series against the Atlanta Braves and force Game 3. The Chicago White Sox followed that up with a sweep of the Houston Astros to become the first wild-card team to move on to the division series.

And there are still two games to go! Will the New York Yankees knock out the rival Boston Red Sox? And can the Chicago Cubs turn on their offense after they were shut out against the San Diego Padres?

We've got you covered with pregame lineups, sights and sounds from the ballparks and postgame takeaways as each Day 2 matchup ends.

Luis Garcia Jr. goes yard

Father and son moment in the Bronx

Takeaways

Chicago White Sox 7, Houston Astros 3
Chicago wins series 2-0

It was over when ... Chase Meidroth took Bryan Abreu deep for a back-breaking three-run blast in the sixth. This came just minutes after it looked like Houston was about to overcome Chicago's early 4-0 edge. With two on in the fifth inning and the lead down to 4-3, Anthony Kay came out of the bullpen to get Yordan Alvarez on a fly to left. After a walk to Isaac Paredes loaded the bases, Jose Altuve flied out to end the threat. After the White Sox drew two walks to start the sixth, Meidroth showed bunt on Abreu's first two offerings. Following a double steal, Meidroth went back to swing mode and launched what turned out to be a series-clinching blast. The White Sox's Cinderella ride continues into the American League Division Series.

Stat that defined the game: Alvarez managed just a lone single in eight at-bats during the brief series, a .125 average to go with some failings in high-leverage spots. He also failed to make a grab on a well-struck Sam Antonacci drive to start the game, something a more mobile left fielder might have caught. Alvarez is still great and on his way to win the AL MVP Award. But it was a rough couple of days for him in the wild-card round. -- Bradford Doolittle

Key moments from Chicago's win:

White Sox win first playoff series since 2005

Chicago breaks game open with huge three-run homer

Altuve joins the fun with Houston's third solo home run of the night

Houston answers with leadoff homer from Peña

Make that four runs in the 1st!

Philadelphia Phillies 4, Atlanta Braves 3
Series tied at 1-1

It was over when ... It appeared to be over when Bryce Harper misplayed Drake Baldwin's relatively routine fly ball that turned into a generously-scored RBI single in the seventh inning to give the Braves a 2-1 lead (and they added another run). But then Kyle Schwarber and Harper hit back-to-back home runs in the eighth off Dylan Lee, who hadn't allowed a home run all season to a left-handed batter. Alec Bohm then hit the game-winning home run in the 10th off Didier Fuentes -- just Bohm's second opposite-field home run all season.

And then it was actually finally over when Andrew Painter struck out Dominic Smith with two runners on in the bottom of the 10th -- on a walk-off challenge on the third strike. The Phillies' season is alive.

Star who defined the game: The Phillies getting to Lee was the big shocker to begin with, and Bohm going to right field was also a shock, but the biggest shocker might have been Painter pitching the scoreless eighth, ninth and 10th innings for the Phillies. With Jhoan Duran having thrown 27 pitches on Tuesday and manager Don Mattingly not trusting anybody else in the bullpen -- which had the worst ERA in the majors in September -- he turned to his rookie, who had started in 23 of his 25 appearances. Gutsy call ... and it worked. -- David Schoenfield

Game 2 starters: Kevin Gausman vs. Nick Pivetta

What the Cubs need to do to force Game 3: Score early. Michael King's gem in Game 1 meant Padres manager Craig Stammen didn't have to utilize Adrian Morejon or Mason Miller. By the time Game 2 rolls around, Morejon and Miller will be coming off three full days of rest, able to provide at least nine outs. No team scored more runs than the Cubs this season, and they'll have to show that against Nick Pivetta in Game 2. It will start, of course, with Pete Crow-Armstrong and Alex Bregman at the top of the lineup. King shut them down in Game 1, striking them out a combined five times. That can't happen again. In hopes of generating more offense, it'll be interesting to see if Bregman plays third base, which would allow the left-handed-hitting Michael Conforto to start at designated hitter. -- Alden Gonzalez

stories.headline: WNBA offseason 2026: Guides for every eliminated team
stories.summary: We're breaking down the biggest questions and offseason needs for every team eliminated in the 2026 WNBA playoffs.
stories.body:
The first team eliminated from the 2026 WNBA playoffs was a shocking one: the No.1 seed Minnesota Lynx, who were swept by the No. 8 New York Liberty in two blowout losses. On Wednesday, the No. 5 Washington Mystics were the second team eliminated following a sweep by the No. 4 Atlanta Dream.

For the Lynx and every other team eliminated this postseason, we're breaking down potential moves for each WNBA franchise, including a look at the state of each roster, team needs and priorities for each front office this coming offseason.

Movement during WNBA free agency in 2027 could be more active than ever given the short turnaround between the new collective bargaining agreement and the start of 2026 training camps.

The draft lottery, typically held in November or December, will determine which team will get the No. 1 pick in the 2027 draft. After three expansion teams joined the WNBA the past two seasons, the league will stick with 15 teams for 2027, but the Connecticut Sun will relocate to Houston.

Eliminated in the first round of the WNBA playoffs

Washington Mystics
2026 regular season: 28-16; No. 5 seed

Postseason results: Swept by No. 4 seed Atlanta in the first round

Free agents: Betnijah Laney-Hamilton (unrestricted)

2027 draft capital: Own first-round pick (can swap with Chicago Sky), two second-round picks (one via Sky), third-round pick

Season recap: This was a dream season for the franchise: It reached the playoffs for the first time since 2023 in just Year 2 of a complete rebuild. Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen were selected for the All-Star Game for the second time in their two-year careers. Shakira Austin made the biggest leap of her career and was in the running for both Most Improved Player and Defensive Player of the Year while setting the franchise record for single-season points scored. The team developed into one of the best defensive units in the league, ranked No. 2 in defensive rating and points allowed. With a foundation built off six first-round picks in the last two drafts, Washington became the youngest team in league history to reach the postseason and had the league's best record after July 20.

State of the roster: The Mystics are in an ideal spot, with everyone but Laney-Hamilton under contract and most of the roster still on rookie deals. Austin is the only player making more than $750,000 per year. There's cap space and plenty of options. The biggest question for team president Michael Winger is whether to continue supplementing the roster with young talent in the draft, or spending money on a big-name veteran to earnestly chase a championship?

Top front office priority: Shooting. Coach Sydney Johnson wants to play fast and shoot 3s, but even as the defense flourished this season, the offense was still a work in progress. The Mystics ranked No. 14 in pace and last in 3-point attempts. That makes sense for a roster where the strength is in its size and athleticism; Austin, Iriafen and Lauren Betts forming one of the biggest frontcourts in the league. Citron's 3-point percentage dipped in 2026, and 2025 No. 6 draft pick Georgia Amoore has room to grow; these were her first pro games after she tore her ACL during training camp of her rookie year. The hope is growth from both players will help, but improving the long-range shooting should be a priority.

Biggest offseason question: At this point of the rebuild, what's next? The Mystics will, again, have a lottery pick from a swap with Chicago. Do they stay on the current path, building through the draft and declining to take a big swing in free agency or at the trade deadline? Are they at a point where the front office is willing to spend on an established entity who would make the Mystics true championship contenders? Or do they believe the natural progression of the youngsters in house is enough to make a legit run at a title? With everyone but Austin on team-friendly deals, the cash is available to add to this roster before they have to start paying out second contracts. -- Kareem Copeland

Minnesota Lynx
2026 regular season: 33-11, No. 1 seed

Postseason result: Swept by No. 8 seed New York in the first round

Free agents: Napheesa Collier (unrestricted), Maya Caldwell (restricted), Dorka Juhasz (reserved), Emma Cechova (reserved), Antonia Delaere (reserved), Chloe Bibby (reserved)

2027 draft capital: Own first- and third-round picks

Season recap: The Lynx hit the 30-win mark for the third season in a row and were the No. 1 seed for the second consecutive year. Olivia Miles was Rookie of the Year, and Cheryl Reeve was Coach of the Year. But the season ended in disappointment with their first-round loss to the Liberty. There were signs, though, that the early exit could happen.

The Lynx over-performed for much of the regular season, led by point guard Miles, who took charge of the offense. A lot was on her shoulders. The Lynx were without star forward Collier (offseason surgery on both ankles) until late July. The Lynx lost forwards Jessica Shepard and Alanna Smith to Dallas in free agency. Cechova, a promising rookie center, was lost to an ACL injury in May after just three games. Forward Juhasz was out until early July with a foot injury. Thus, the Lynx had to rely a lot on veteran forwards Natasha Howard and Nia Brodie, and guard play led by Miles, and veterans Kayla McBride and Courtney Williams.

Minnesota lost four of its last six regular-season games and didn't improve its level of play in the latter part of the regular season or postseason. Meanwhile, the up-and-down Liberty, one of the preseason favorites to win the WNBA title, were an unlikely No. 8 seed with a record that didn't reflect how good they could be. The best version of the Liberty showed up at the worst time for Minnesota.

State of the roster: Miles is a great young building block who will be on the second year of her rookie contract in 2027. She is already one of the WNBA's most exciting players. McBride, Williams, Howard and Brodie are all signed for next season, too. But Collier, who has been with the Lynx her entire career, is a free agent. Her decision on whether to stay in Minnesota will make an enormous difference in the direction of the Lynx's future.

Top front office priority: Re-signing Collier, or figuring out how to go forward without her.

Biggest offseason question: If Collier returns to the Lynx, the key question is what else they need to win the franchise's fifth championship. They came close in 2024, falling in overtime in the last game of the WNBA Finals at New York. An injury to Collier cost them in their 2024 semifinal loss to Phoenix. And this year, they were a better team for the first four months of the season than they were the last month.

If Collier does not return, the Lynx must start a different era and likely will need to go into free agency or trade for more post talent. -- Michael Voepel

Eliminated in the regular season
All stats for teams eliminated in the regular season are through Aug. 30, when the FIBA break started.

Portland Fire
2026 season: Eliminated from playoff race

Free agents: Karlie Samuelson (unrestricted), Emily Englster (restricted), Nika Muhl (club option)

2027 draft capital: Own first- and second-round picks

Season recap: The Fire were eliminated from playoff contention with six games left on their schedule but have had a solid inaugural season. Portland put together signature wins against Indiana, New York and Dallas, but growing pains were still evident. The Fire couldn't string together more than three wins in a row (in May), suffered a four-game losing streak in June and a five-game skid in July. Following coach Alex Sarama's Constraints-Led Approach, the Fire have a clear identity built on instinct and offensive fluidity, and they produced the eighth-best offense in the league. But their defense ranks second to last. Bridget Carleton, Sarah Ashlee Barker and Carla Leite -- who were all selected in the expansion draft -- had breakout seasons, giving Portland a solid future to build on.

State of the roster: Portland should return next season with several players who were key contributors to its inaugural year in Carleton, Megan DiLeo and Leite, and the hope is that Barker makes a full recovery from a torn ACL suffered in July. It all gives the Fire great continuity to build upon their success heading into Year 2 -- exactly what an expansion franchise wants.

Top front office priority: An elite shot creator and go-to bucket getter. Portland emphasizes the development of players already on its roster, but that shouldn't hold it back from adding that kind of player. Leite has been the Fire's leading scorer this season, averaging 15.9 points per game, with an incredible ability to drive to the bucket and finish. Carleton and Barker have shot decently from distance, but if they want to take their quick-paced offense to the next level, the Fire should add a veteran scorer. Portland would also benefit in adding a true center to help down low.

Biggest offseason question: Can Portland improve enough in Year 2 to make the postseason? Perhaps Golden State set unfair standards for what should be expected from a current-day expansion franchise -- making the playoffs in both of its first two seasons. The Fire can choose to run it back with the same group, but they could benefit from taking a swing for a big signing. -- Kendra Andrews

Chicago Sky

2026 season: Eliminated from playoff race

Free agents: DiJonai Carrington (unrestricted), Natasha Cloud (unrestricted), Rachel Banham (unrestricted), Sydney Taylor (reserved)

2027 draft capital: Own two first-round picks (including one via Atlanta), but Washington owns swap rights for one; third-round pick

Season recap: There was all the optimism in the world after a 3-1 start with wins over Golden State and Minnesota. Everything changed when 2024 No. 4 draft pick Rickea Jackson -- traded from the Sparks for Ariel Atkins -- was lost to a torn ACL in the fourth game of the season after she averaged career highs in points (18.0), rebounds (4.8), assists (2.0) and blocks (1.8). The Sky were never the same afterward as they lost 11 of the next 12 games. Jackson wasn't the only injury as Chicago leads the league with 127 games missed, according to The IX Sports injury tracker. Azura Stevens, Carrington, Courtney Vandersloot, Skylar Diggins, Gabriela Jaquez, Cloud and Taylor all missed time. Diggins never returned after July 3.

After that 1-12 stretch, the Sky hovered just below .500 the rest of the way as Taylor developed into one of the top rookie scorers in the league despite going undrafted. Cloud is having a career shooting year and Kamilla Cardoso continues her incremental growth. They weren't an easy out as of late June, but struggled with defense and consistency.

State of the roster: Diggins, Stevens, Vandersloot, Cardoso, Jackson, Elizabeth Williams, Jacy Sheldon and Jaquez are all signed through 2027. That's the core that general manager Jeff Pagliocca was excited about heading into 2026. Carrington, Cloud and Banham are unrestricted free agents. The salary cap was $7 million in 2026 and is able to move up or down by no more than 13% in 2027. As of now, and if the cap remains the same, Chicago would have about $1.8 million in cap space with eight players currently under contract.

Top front office priority: Pagliocca does not believe in tearing things down to the studs to rebuild. So, despite missing the playoffs for the third consecutive season, don't expect a youth movement to start over. The biggest acquisition is likely to be the return of Jackson. Shooting was a minus this season as the Sky rank No. 13 in 3-point percentage (29.2%) and No. 10 in field goal percentage (44.1%). They also need more stops after ranking No. 11 in the league in scoring defense (89.7). With Diggins out, Taylor was often the only player able to create her own quality looks late in the shot clock or games.

Biggest offseason question: The health of Jackson and the mindset of Diggins. Jackson was looking like the league's most improved player before the injury. When will she be ready and how long will it take to return to that level of play? The other question is where Diggins stands mentally with the team. She talked about the team's "loser mentality" in early June and also pointed to coach Tyler Marsh when questioned about the struggling half-court offense. Diggins acknowledged "an extremely frustrating experience." On July 6, the seven-time All-Star took to social media to announce that she'd been benched. She never played another game after July 3, officially due to a knee injury. However, Diggins confirmed that she hasn't asked for nor is looking for a trade. She sounded committed to the team despite the previous frustrations, which included the practice facility not being completed in 2026. -- Kareem Copeland

Los Angeles Sparks

2026 season: Eliminated from playoff race

Free agents: Rae Burrell (restricted), Emma Cannon (unrestricted)

2027 draft capital: Own two first-round picks (including via Phoenix), two second-round picks (including via Storm) and third-round pick

Season recap: The Sparks were confident this would be the year they finally broke the five-year playoff drought. But currently sitting in 11th place in the standings, Los Angeles missed the postseason for the sixth year in a row as it struggled to find consistency. The positive early on: Kelsey Plum was playing at an MVP level and led the league in scoring. But an injury sidelined her for over a month, and then the Sparks sent her to Phoenix at the trade deadline. The Sparks also played without Cameron Brink for nine games. L.A. suffered six consecutive losses in mid-July, and another six-game skid in August, leading to the firing of former general manager Raegan Pebley.

State of the roster: The Sparks have five players under contract heading into the 2027 season: Ariel Atkins, Dearica Hamby, Erica Wheeler, Brink and Monique Akoa Makani. Nneka Ogwumike announced her plans to retire after this season, leaving a massive hole.

Top front office priority: Pick a direction. The Sparks split ways with Pebley after yet another underwhelming season. Pebley's tenure with Los Angeles was defined by win-now moves in an effort to bring back the historical dominance that the Sparks are tied to, but each fell short. With Pebley gone, Ogwumike retiring and Plum traded, the Sparks' front office -- Ariana Andonian, a former general manager and vice president of player personnel for the Philadelphia 76ers' G League affiliate, was named Sparks GM on Friday -- has to decide if the organization still wants to make moves it believes will help the team win immediately -- or if it is time for a major shake-up from top to bottom.

Biggest offseason question: Can they sign another coveted free agent? The Sparks have a good track record of landing some of the best players on the market -- most recently signing Plum in 2025 -- but with the recent turbulence the franchise has faced, and the now six-year playoff drought, can they do it again? If the Sparks choose the "win-now" direction mentioned above, they will have to figure out how they can get premier talent to fill out the roster. But it's not certain whether Los Angeles is still seen as a desirable location. -- Andrews

Phoenix Mercury

2026 season: Eliminated from playoff race

Free agents: Kelsey Plum (unrestricted). Valeriane Ayayi (reserved), Kyara Linskens (reserved), Noemie Brochant (reserved), Jovana Nogic (reserved), Lexi Held (reserved), Marta Suarez (reserved), Maddy Westbeld (reserved)

2027 draft capital: Own second- and third-round picks

Season recap: The 2026 season was an absolute disaster coming off a trip to the Finals in 2025. Satou Sabally -- the team's leading scorer with 16.3 points per game in 2025 -- left in free agency and the Mercury didn't add a prolific third running mate for Alyssa Thomas and Kahleah Copper until getting Plum at the trade deadline. Then Plum played only five games due to injury. Sami Whitcomb, who was one of the best reserves in the league in 2025, played less than half the season. DeWanna Bonner moved into the starting lineup, but that wasn't enough. The team ended up buying out Bonner in August to allow her to join a playoff team, which ended up being Atlanta. Nearly every metric measures the Mercury as a below-average offense, and things aren't better defensively, as they are one of the worst rebounding teams in the league. The defense is allowing seven more points per game from 2025 to 2026.

State of the roster: With only Copper, Thomas, Whitcomb and Natasha Mack under contract for 2027, Phoenix has the flexibility to retool the roster. Coach Nate Tibbetts will be going into his fourth season and coming off his worst since he was hired as the highest-paid coach in league history. Going from the Finals to the lottery is the wrong direction, though he didn't have as talented of a roster in 2026. With all of the recent investments into the organization, the leash might not be particularly long for anyone if the Mercury aren't back in the playoffs in 2027. Thomas remains one of the elite players in the league, but she'll turn 35 in April, and the end of her career is much closer than the beginning. Time is of the essence for the organization to return to the pinnacle with Thomas still playing at this level.

Top front office priority: Keeping Plum is the first, second and third priority. Everything hinges on getting Plum to sign after giving up a first- and second-round pick and Monique Akoa Makani. That's a lottery pick gone in what's expected to be a quality draft. Losing that for five games of sub-100% Plum would be a horrible trade and set the franchise back for the future. Acquiring Plum probably enhances the opportunity of signing other talent looking to make a run at a championship. The five-time All-Star has two championship rings with the Aces. Her decision will go a long way to determine the Mercury's offseason success. The Mercury took a big swing and are still waiting to find out the results.

Biggest offseason question: Can the Mercury return to championship contention? The biggest factor to answering that question is another: Will Plum return? This is an organization with a win-now mindset, and hovering near the bottom of the standings was unacceptable. The hiring of Tibbetts, the finished practice facility, trading for Thomas and Copper before the 2025 season and trading for Plum were all moves aimed at winning a title. Can general manager Nick U'Ren keep Plum, tweak the roster and quickly return to contention? Plum's decision will likely have the biggest impact on such. -- Copeland

Toronto Tempo

2026 season: Eliminated from playoff race

Free agents: Temi Fagbenle (unrestricted), Isabelle Harrison (unrestricted), Kia Nurse (unrestricted), Nyara Sabally (restricted), Maria Conde (reserved), Laura Juskaite (reserved)

2027 draft capital: Own first-, second- and third-round picks

Season recap: The Tempo were a .500 team and rolling along before Brittney Sykes was lost for most of the season with a plantar fascia injury. Sykes and Marina Mabrey combined to form one of the highest-scoring backcourts in the league as both were in the midst of career years. Including the game when Sykes went down, Toronto went 4-21 from that point, including a 12-game losing streak. A Grade 2 left ankle sprain suffered by rookie Kiki Rice kept the team's third-leading scorer off the floor for nearly two months. Sabally and Harrison also missed stretches due to injury. The Tempo added a young big in 2025 No. 7 draft pick Aneesah Morrow in a trade with the Sun for Maria Kliundikova and a 2028 second-round pick. As a group, the team seemed ahead of expectations under two-time championship-winning coach Sandy Brondello, but the losses piled up without Sykes and as other injuries depleted the roster.

State of the roster: The combination of Mabrey, Sykes and Rice on the perimeter is a strong foundation on which to build. There's plenty of flexibility between expiring deals and cap room to continue to tweak the roster. Julie Allemand, Morrow and Teonni Key are all under contract for 2027. Rice looks like a budding franchise cornerstone and will certainly be an All-Rookie selection.

Top front office priority: Depth and talent in the frontcourt. Harrison is an unrestricted free agent with injury history. Sabally is restricted, and has been injury-prone throughout her career and, again, missed nearly half the season in 2026. However, the 2022 No. 5 draft pick put together a career year with 12.3 points and 5.3 rebounds per game when she was on the floor. Sabally also has a coach who believes in her in Brondello, who was at the helm of the Liberty when the team drafted her. So, there are some decisions to be made in terms of their own free agents and how to build out the rest of the roster. The Tempo are one of four teams that have had at least 100 games missed due to injury, so that added another challenge to evaluating the organization's inaugural year.

Biggest offseason question: There are few expectations on an expansion franchise in the early years. The biggest question: Was the fast start to 2026 a fluke or a sign of what could be when healthy? As Kendra wrote above, the Valkyries put pressure on all the following expansion teams after reaching the playoffs in their first year and becoming a contender in Year No. 2. The 2026 season didn't quite show the entire vision for how the Tempo want to look on the floor. -- Copeland

Connecticut Sun

The franchise will relocate to the Houston Comets in the offseason.

2026 season: Eliminated from playoff race

Free agents: Brittney Griner (unrestricted), Kennedy Burke (unrestricted), Diamond Miller (restricted), Raegan Beers (reserved), Ashlon Jackson (reserved)

2027 draft capital: Own first-, second- and third-round picks, plus additional third-round pick (via Portland)

Season recap: It was a weird season in Connecticut, the final for the Sun franchise. The team struggled early with a 2-15 start, not helped by uneven player availability. Standout point guard Leila Lacan missed time due to overseas commitments, while Griner dealt with injuries much of the season. Aneesah Morrow then fell out of the rotation and was traded at the deadline to Toronto for the rights to Maria Kliundikova and a 2028 second-round pick. The Sun were better later in the summer, but the reality of the franchise's impending relocation put a damper on the atmosphere around Uncasville.

State of the roster: The Houston front office has plenty of young talent it can choose to build around between Lacan and Saniya Rivers, as well as Gianna Kneepkens, Charlisse Leger-Walker and Nell Angloma, who are all either rookies or second-year players. Olivia Nelson-Ododa and Aaliyah Edwards are also under contract, and both took some positive steps forward in 2026. In all, that offers plenty of flexibility for the resurgent Houston franchise to construct its first roster.

Top front office priority: From the front office down to basketball operations, there's little known so far about the Houston team's identity and philosophy moving forward, including how many Sun personnel will move with the team. But presumably the biggest goal will be to build around the team's upcoming lottery pick. The team will no doubt want to also put its best foot forward in talking to free agents this winter, whether that results in signing players for 2027 or laying the groundwork for the future.

Biggest offseason question: Will JuJu Watkins declare for the WNBA draft? Houston currently has the best odds of winning the No. 1 pick, so if the ping-pong balls fall in its favor, and the transcendent Watkins -- who has additional eligibility beyond this upcoming college season -- goes pro, that would be best-case scenario on and off the court as Houston returns to the WNBA. -- Alexa Philippou

Seattle Storm

2026 season: Eliminated from playoff race

Free agents: Stefanie Dolson (unrestricted), Zia Cooke (restricted), Jade Melbourne (restricted), Mackenzie Holmes (reserved), Jordan Horston (reserved), Taylor Thierry (reserved)

2027 draft capital: Own first- and third-round picks, plus additional third-round pick (via Dallas); also swap rights for Indiana's third-round pick

Season recap: After Seattle came within one missed shot of upsetting eventual champion Las Vegas in the first round of the playoffs last season, a ton changed for the Storm. They parted ways with coach Noelle Quinn after five seasons and hired Sonia Raman. Their top five scorers, led by forward Nneka Ogwumike and guard Skylar Diggins, left in free agency. Seattle's leading returning scorer, forward Ezi Magbegor, didn't play until July 2 due to a foot injury. And the 2025 No. 2 draft pick, center Dominique Malonga, missed eight games early on due to concussion protocol.

Seattle ownership and fans knew that this would be a rebuilding season in which the Storm would get court time for a lot of young players, including center Awa Fam, the No. 3 draft pick, and guard Flau'jae Johnson, the No. 8 pick. The Storm's lack of experience showed up most on offense, as they are near the bottom of the league in offensive rating (an estimate of points scored per 100 possessions). The Storm did a little better defensively, especially with inside enforcers such as Magbegor, Malonga and Fam, all of whom are 6-foot-4 or taller. Overall, though, there will be no surprise about Seattle's final record. This season was about improving for the future.

State of the roster: If it's healthy, a good core will return for Seattle. Guard Natisha Hiedeman, Magbegor, Malonga, Fam and Johnson are all signed for 2027. Hiedeman is the oldest of that group; she turns 30 in February 2027.

Top front office priority: The franchise that was defined by point guard Sue Bird for two decades now needs a point guard. The Storm are near the top of the league in turnovers this season, while being near the bottom in assists. That's a bad formula for seeking success. Seattle has the potential for a dominant front line, especially with Malonga and Fam being just 20 years old with vast potential. So either through free agency, a trade or the draft, Seattle could use an elite point guard who can maximize what the post players can do.

Biggest offseason question: Can the Storm get back to the playoffs in 2027? This is just the fourth time they have missed the postseason since 2004, when they won their first of four WNBA titles. If Seattle can get the right floor general and keep its best players healthy in 2027, the Storm have a chance to be back in the postseason mix where they are used to being. -- Michael Voepel

stories.headline: Sean McVay: NFL told Rams DPI shouldn't have been called
stories.summary: Rams head coach Sean McVay says the NFL told the team that defensive pass interference should not have been called against cornerback Josh Wallace in Sunday night's loss to the Broncos.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Rams coach Sean McVay said Wednesday that the NFL told the team that defensive pass interference should not have been called against cornerback Josh Wallace in Sunday night's loss to the Denver Broncos.

The play came on third-and-6 from the Los Angeles 11, when Wallace intercepted a pass by Broncos quarterback Bo Nix. The cornerback was called for defensive pass interference on Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant, giving Denver first-and-goal at the 7. The Broncos scored on the drive to take a 30-26 lead with 47 seconds left.

McVay said Monday that the team turned the play into the league in an effort to get clarity on the call, saying, "The most important intent is making sure we educate our players on how it's being officiated so there's clarity of how we can coach them to play technique and fundamentally through the cycle of the snap."

On Wednesday, McVay said the league "agreed" with him that the penalty should not have been called.

"The goal is to just get good, consistent feedback," McVay said. "It doesn't matter. Like I've told you, the only thing that matters to me is how to educate our players. ... Whether it was or wasn't right, that wasn't the point. The call was made and that was what the call was. What I am interested in is if there's any sort of feedback that says this is in alignment with what would be correctly officiated as a DPI, here's the coaching points that you want your DBs or your backend guys to be able to have.

"That's the only thing that I'm really worried about. That game's over with. We're a 1-2 football team and got to be able to move forward."

The Rams' next chance to do that comes Sunday against the 2-1 Philadelphia Eagles. McVay said the team expects to have wide receiver Puka Nacua back for the game. Nacua, who has sat out the past two games because of soreness in his groin, returned to practice Wednesday and was limited.

Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald, who came out of retirement in late August, did not practice Wednesday. McVay said Donald is dealing with a sore back but said it is too early to determine whether it will affect his game status for Week 4.

"Just taking it a day at a time," McVay said. "I wouldn't want to say anything of that nature yet, but I think the back's a little bit sore. And he's as tough as it gets, and so I'll continue to have updates as the week goes."

stories.headline: Golden Knights sign C William Karlsson to 2-year, $13.5M deal
stories.summary: The Vegas Golden Knights have locked in center William Karlsson on a two-year extension with an AAV of $6.75 million.
stories.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights have locked in center William Karlsson on a two-year extension with an AAV of $6.75 million, the club announced on Wednesday. That will keep Karlsson -- one of Vegas' original "Golden Misfits" -- with the team through 2028-29.

Karlsson, 33, joined the Golden Knights from Columbus in the 2017 expansion draft. He dressed in 570 regular season games for the franchise and ranks second in goals (156) and points (403) for the organization since their inaugural 2017-18 campaign. Karlsson helped the Golden Knights to a Stanley Cup victory in 2023, appearing in 22 games with 17 points.

Vegas has missed Karlsson for chunks of the last two seasons due to various injuries. He was limited to just 53 games in 2024-25 and then was sidelined after just 14 games in 2025-26 with a lower-body injury that kept Karlsson sidelined for the final 68 regular season tilts.

He was able to return for the playoffs though and suited up in 15 games to push Vegas into another Stanley Cup Final -- but Karlsson was injured in Game 5 and did not dress for Game 6, where the Golden Knights lost to Carolina.

When Karlsson is healthy, he's been a strong two-way performer for Vegas with great defensive upside and is perennially one of the club's most dangerous penalty killers. While Karlsson's offensive stats have lagged since a career-high 43 goal showing in 2017-18, he remains a good complement to Mitch Marner and Brett Howden on Vegas' second line heading into the just-launched 2026-27 campaign.

stories.headline: 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey: 'I want to be judged by winning'
stories.summary: Coming off a career year, Tyrese Maxey said he doesn't want to be judged by how he does individually but by how the 76ers do as a team this year.
stories.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- Having earned two All-Star nods in the last three seasons and coming off a campaign in which he averaged a career-high 28.3 points per game, Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey is primed for another big year.

But the 25-year-old said Wednesday after the Sixers' second practice of training camp that the only metric he cares about for Philadelphia's highly anticipated upcoming season is team success.

"I'm at the point now where I've showed what I can do talent-wise," Maxey said. "Of course, I'm going to continue to get better, but I want to be judged by winning. If we win, that's what I want to be judged by. That's really my main mindset, my main goal, is finding ways to win."

Maxey was the first of Philly's four major stars -- including Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and LeBron James -- to speak to reporters since training camp started Tuesday.

Brown sidestepped a query on media day Monday when asked about how the Sixers will determine a pecking order and identify an "alpha" by replying: "Next question."

Maxey's answer was in the same spirit, albeit much more elaborate, as he detailed his willingness to adjust to help the team.

"Because I've played so many different roles, I'm capable of doing so many different things," Maxey said. "And I think that's going to be a positive for myself and for this team. I can play on the ball. I can play off the ball. I can play in transition. I can catch and shoot. Play off [of] pin downs. I can play pick-and-roll. ...

"I'm going to play however they need me to play. However Coach [Nick Nurse] wants to play, that's how I'm going to play."

And Maxey is not only leading by example. He is speaking up as the new group gets off the ground.

"My voice carries a little bit and then just the charisma of me smiling and having a good time," Maxey said. "I mean, I'm getting older ... and I just feel like I've been here for a minute. Process [Embiid] has been here, I think what, 13 years? I've been here seven. So, we've been here for a while, kind of know how things go around here and just am trying to keep using my voice and help everybody get familiar and help everybody get comfortable."

Beyond vowing to acquiesce to any role change that is asked of him, Maxey also used his voice to be effusive in his praise of the other stars on the team in his answers Wednesday.

On James: "That's like a big brother to me. He's an old man ... He's a good guy. He's a good guy."

On Embiid: "He looks amazing. He looks happy. ... When you're healthy and you're happy and you're at peace with your life and basketball, that's when you're at your best. He's been great."

On Brown: "JB's like physically a freak of nature. He's just stronger than you. He jumps higher than you. He's faster than you and he's very talented. Those are the things that you see every single day. And I think what's stood out to me so far is his communication and he's willing to pick up the ball defensively, kind of just do whatever coach needs him to do right now."

Brown was the last player on the court after practice, working on handling double teams in the post - by kicking out to a shooter or fading away for a jumper along the baseline - with a massive Sixers logo on the wall of the practice facility behind him.

Maxey made sure to acknowledge the transition for Brown, too, as he begins life with the Sixers after having played for the Boston Celtics for his entire career before being traded within the Atlantic Division in July.

"This is very foreign to him, imagine being somewhere for [10] years and coming here, the team that you're trained to hate, probably," Maxey said. "It's been great. Especially [since] we just beat [Boston in the playoffs]. It's kind of crazy."

stories.headline: Philadelphia Union, USMNT's Cavan Sullivan becomes youngest MLS Player of the Month
stories.summary: Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.
stories.body:
Philadelphia Union and United States men's national team midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.

At 16, Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player to start a game for the United States since Freddy Adu in 2006 when he was picked in Mauricio Pochettino's XI for Saturday's 4-1 friendly win vs. Peru.

He was one of 11 players -- including seven other teenagers -- to make their first appearances for the U.S. in that game against Peru.

Sullivan, who turned 17 on Sept. 28, came on as a substitute on Tuesday in the USMNT's 4-2 friendly win over Chile.

Sullivan has seven goals and 12 assists in 26 games for the Union, who have surged up to sixth place in the Eastern Conference in recent weeks. He has played 1,675 league minutes in MLS.

His 19 goal contributions are tied with Alphonso Davies (2018) for the second-most by a teenager in an MLS season, trailing only Diego Fagundez (20 in 2013).

Since returning from the World Cup break, the Union have recorded 32 points during a 12-game unbeaten streak, which is tied for the most points by a club in a 12-game span in MLS history. Sullivan has started all 11 of those games, logging a goal contribution in eight of them.

Sullivan and the Union will return after the FIFA international break on Oc. 10 to host Real Salt Lake at Subaru Park (7:30 p.m. ET).

stories.headline: Ayrton Senna's Honda NSX could fetch £800,000 at London auction
stories.summary: A 1991 Honda NSX that once belonged to Ayrton Senna will go up for auction in London at the end of October.
stories.body:
A 1991 Honda NSX that once belonged to Ayrton Senna will go up for auction in London at the end of October.

Chassis number T000233 was one of three NSXs delivered to Senna as part of his contract with Honda in the early 1990s and, due to its provenance, carries an estimate of £500,000 to £800,000.

When the car first went on sale in 1990 it had a list price of between £52,000 and £55,000, with low-mileage NSXs from the same era currently listed online for up to £135,000.

The legendary Japanese sports car is closely linked to Senna, who contributed to its development before it went on sale as Honda's answer to the more expensive Porsche and Ferrari sportscars of the era.

Chassis T000233 is finished in Formula Red over a black leather interior and was delivered to Portugal in March 1991 so that Senna could make use of it while staying at his property in Quinta do Lago.

According to the listing on Sotheby's website, the NSX featured in the 1992 documentary, 'Ayrton Senna: Racing Is In My Blood' and was used by the Brazilian to commute to the 1991 Portuguese Grand Prix in Estoril.

Senna, who died in an accident at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix, won all three of his world titles with Honda power while racing at McLaren.

stories.headline: Former draftee slams AFL over concussion plight
stories.summary: An AFL draftee whose life was upended by a concussion injury says he "was so close to ending everything".
stories.body:
An AFL draftee whose life was upended by a concussion injury says he "was so close to ending everything".

Aiden O'Driscoll, who had to retire because of a devastating training injury without making his AFL debut, also slammed the league as an "absolute joke".

"The last couple of years I've experienced nothing but pain, and I've explained it multiple times to you. You're supposed to help AFL players through hardship, not leave them with absolutely nothing," O'Driscoll wrote in his extensive Instagram post.

His comments came a day after Geelong announced defender Jake Kolodjashnij had retired.

Last month, the Cats were fined $140,000 and current AFL chairman Craig Drummond apologised after it emerged the club had agreed to a secret concussion waiver with Kolodjashnij. Drummond was Geelong president at the time the agreement was struck.

The Geelong controversy highlighted the complexity and sensitivity around contact sport's concussion crisis.

The Western Bulldogs recruited O'Driscoll in the 2023 draft. But a head injury that summer left him with significant ongoing health problems and the club announced in May, 2024 that he had retired on medical grounds.

"The doctors described my concussion as 'one of the worst' they've seen, with eight micro brain bleeds, and (a) fracture behind my ear," O'Driscoll wrote.

"From a medical point of view, losing my career, my identity plus going through the symptoms I have, you'd think the AFL would be useful with some support?

O'Driscoll added it took the AFL six weeks to find him a psychologist.

"Through this period, I was grieving the most, it got to the point where I started questioning my life? If it was worth living?," he wrote.

"I was so close to ending everything, I would've been free from all the pain/trauma. My family/close friends and partners honestly kept me here."

Melbourne premiership player Angus Brayshaw also had to retire in 2024 because of his concussion issues.

In his emotional toast to other retiring players at the Brownlow Medal function that year, Brayshaw referred to O'Driscoll by name.

"I know a few other past players that are dealing with the same issues as I am," O'Driscoll said.

"AFL it's time to step up! I'm a 21-year-old that can't keep suffering each week. While you're at it, help the other past players that need support."

O'Driscoll added he had been told at 18 never to play contact sport again.

The AFL and the players' association were contacted for comment.

stories.headline: Cleary completes golden set with Dally M triumph
stories.summary: Nathan Cleary has completed rugby league's boxed set, with the Penrith star claiming his maiden Dally M Medal after romping to a dominant victory at the NRL's gala night.
stories.body:
Nathan Cleary's rugby league box set is complete, with the Penrith star claiming his maiden Dally M Medal after romping to a dominant victory at the NRL's gala night.

Unable to attend after his horror ankle injury in Penrith's preliminary final loss, Cleary accepted Wednesday night's award from his couch.

The Panthers champion finished 14 points clear of Cronulla half Braydon Trindall, who was in the hunt until a dislocated shoulder ended his regular season.

Tamika Upton also claimed her third Dally M Medal as NRLW player of the year, defending her crown from last year when the Brisbane fullback became the award's first multiple winner.

Warriors mentor Andrew Webster pipped Justin Holbrook to be the NRL's coach of the year with finals not counted, while Canberra playmaker Ethan Sanders was rookie of the year.

But the story of the night was Cleary, who left hospital on Wednesday after undergoing emergency surgery on his ankle.

Despite being the best player of this decade, the Dally M had somehow evaded Cleary due to a run of injuries or suspensions.

But he played 23 games this year, setting up 29 tries and acting as the chief architect of Penrith's run to a preliminary final.

Cleary led the race for the majority of the year, polling 67 votes ahead of Trindall's 53 and Panther Dylan Edwards' 52.

"I can't thank everyone enough for the messages they've sent through and the support I've felt," Cleary said.

"In terms of being able to win the Dally M award, I'm super grateful for that as well.

"I want to start off by thanking all my teammates. None of this would be possible without them. They definitely made me 10,000 times the player that I am."

Cleary had earlier this year claimed his maiden Wally Lewis Medal, silencing his critics by leading NSW to a 2-1 State of Origin series victory.

The 28-year-old has also won two Clive Churchill Medals to go with his four premierships at Penrith.

Meanwhile, Newcastle's magical run to the grand final was not reflected in the Dally M team of the year, with the Knights having no players in the side.

Kalyn Ponga also missed out on captain of the year and Holbrook as coach, with all voting complete at the end of the regular season, when the Knights finished seventh.

Robert Toia and Naufahu Whyte were the two Sydney Roosters representatives named in the side.

In the NRLW, Upton's win came after she polled six points in the penultimate round and then one point in Round 11 to beat Wests Tigers' half Raecene McGregor.

The Broncos No.1 is now the clear best player in the women's game over the opening eight years of the NRLW.

"I've still got lots to improve on," Upton said, with Sunday's grand final against Sydney Roosters still looming.

"We've seen that this year. I have been learning being a sole captain this year.

"We went through a tricky patch this year and I learnt a lot about myself as an individual, but a footy player as well."

Newcastle winger Mercedez Taulelei-Siala was named rookie of the year, after a season when she scored 13 tries in 12 games. Gold Coast mentor Karyn Murphy won the coach's medal.

The heart-touching moment of the night came when South Sydney's Jai Arrow was presented the Peter Frilingos headline moment and the Provan-Summons spirit of the game award for the way he has approached his battle with motor neurone disease.

stories.headline: White Sox sweep Astros for first playoff series win since 2005
stories.summary: The White Sox finished off the Astros with a 7-3 win Wednesday to secure their first playoff series win since beating Houston in the 2005 World Series.
stories.body:
HOUSTON -- The Chicago White Sox used a big first inning and a three-run homer from Chase Meidroth to propel them to a 7-3 win over the Houston Astros on Wednesday to sweep their American League Wild Card Series.

It's the first time Chicago has won a playoff series since beating Houston in the World Series in 2005. Under the direction of second-year skipper Will Venable and with a letter of support from Pope Leo XIV, the White Sox advanced to face AL Central champion Cleveland in the AL Division Series beginning Saturday in Cleveland.

The White Sox, who lost 100 games in each of the past three seasons, are the only team in major league history to follow consecutive 100-loss seasons with a playoff berth.

The AL West-winning Astros went 81-81 to become the first team to reach the postseason without a winning record. Their recent playoff woes in Houston continued Wednesday as they dropped their ninth straight home playoff game in a ninth trip to the postseason in the past 10 years.

Chicago pounced on the Astros for four runs in the first inning a day after scoring three in the first two innings of a 6-3 win. Houston ace Hunter Brown was lifted after getting only two outs and wasn't helped by a sloppy defense that committed two first-inning errors.

He was 6-0 with a 2.39 ERA in six career starts against the White Sox before Wednesday's debacle.

The Astros clawed their way back into it with solo home runs from Jeremy Pena, Cam Smith and Jose Altuve to trail by 1 entering the sixth inning.

AJ Blubaugh, who opened Game 1, and Peter Lambert, pitching on two days' rest, combined to retire the next 13 batters after Brown exited. Chicago's next baserunner came when Lambert walked Andrew Benintendi to start the sixth and then walked Tristan Peters.

Bryan Abreu came in, and Meidroth smashed his fifth pitch off the wall in left field to push the lead to 7-3. He yelled on his entire trip around the bases to the delight of a patch of White Sox fans seated near the visitors dugout.

Houston faced boos for a second game in a row from an unusually thin crowd. It's a second straight playoff trip in which the Astros have been swept at home in the wild card after losing both games to Detroit in 2024.

Now they'll face an uncertain future with manager Joe Espada's contract set to expire at season's end after general manager Dana Brown was fired last month.

It was a disappointing series for Houston slugger and AL MVP favorite Yordan Alvarez, who managed only a single with two strikeouts in eight at-bats in the series.

Altuve's shot to the seats in left field in the fourth inning got the Astros to within 4-3. It was the 28th postseason homer of his career, which is second in MLB history behind Manny Ramirez (29).

The Astros had a shot to take the lead before Meidroth's homer. They loaded the bases with two outs in the fifth, but Anthony Kay retired Altuve on a fly out to end the inning.

stories.headline: Patriots' Drake Maye: Shoulder fine, all OK with Mike Vrabel
stories.summary: Drake Maye said Wednesday the physical condition of his right shoulder hasn't affected his throwing ability, instead highlighting the need to make better decisions to reverse his early-season struggles in the Patriots' 1-2 start.
stories.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Quarterback Drake Maye said Wednesday the physical condition of his right shoulder hasn't affected his throwing ability, instead highlighting the need to make better decisions to reverse his early-season struggles in the New England Patriots' 1-2 start.

"That's what makes and breaks play for quarterbacks," Maye said after the team's first practice in preparation for Sunday's road game against the AFC East-leading Buffalo Bills (3-0).

"I don't feel like we're struggling to move the ball. I think we're turning the football over, doing things that are preventing us from scoring touchdowns, and I think that's one of the biggest things for me."

At the same time, Maye was listed on the injury report for the first time this season due to his right throwing shoulder. He was a full participant in practice Wednesday.

"I felt good out there today," he said. "I think we've had a history of good football when we don't turn the football over, so that's the biggest thing, and I'm looking forward to another good week of practice."

Maye has completed 63.8% of his passes, with six interceptions, one lost fumble and just one touchdown pass.

In Sunday's 35-6 loss to the Jaguars, he was sacked three times and also rushed four times for 18 yards. After the game, he was asked if he has felt any lingering effects from the right shoulder injury he suffered in the AFC Championship Game that led to him taking a pain-killing injection before Super Bowl LX.

"I wouldn't say there is a problem with my shoulder," Maye answered, adding, "You're going to get banged up every now and then, but at the same time, a lot of guys are banged up."

Maye, along with coach Mike Vrabel, also fielded questions Wednesday regarding their working relationship. After Maye's third turnover Sunday in Jacksonville, Vrabel wrapped his arms around Maye's shoulder pads on the sideline.

"Coach Vrabel's been one of the best football coaches I've had in my life," Maye said. "I've loved playing for him, and it's not going to change. The way he pushes me, and he coaches the quarterbacks in a way that I really respect, and I'm looking forward to getting going, proving to Coach that I can lead this football team and play good football."

Early in Wednesday's practice, Vrabel approached Maye during a stretching period for a chat.

"I had choices as to where I wanted to coach. I wanted to coach here because Drake was the quarterback," Vrabel said Wednesday.

stories.headline: Klopp not preparing for more titles after verdict against Man City
stories.summary: Jürgen Klopp said Wednesday he would "wait and see" before commenting on the Premier League's announcement yesterday that Manchester City had been found guilty of 114 charges for breaching financial rules.
stories.body:
Jürgen Klopp said Wednesday he would wait to see how things pan out before commenting on the Premier League's announcement yesterday that Manchester City had been found guilty of 114 charges for breaching financial rules.

The charges cover a period between 2009 and 2018, with Klopp's tenure at Liverpool -- which began in 2015 -- overlapping with the time that City were have found to be guilty of breaking Premier League rules.

On the eve of Germany's match against Serbia in the Nations League, though, Klopp seemed content to let his record at Merseyside speak for itself instead of speculating over what might have been.

"I haven't given it much thought, even though I've seen it of course," Klopp said. "Should any sanctions be imposed, I naturally have nothing to do with it anyway, and that's why I'm waiting to see how things pan out. But when you're talking about legal proceedings that have been going on for so long now, I assume there will be an appeal or something like that? That will take ages again of course.

"So I'm a long way from preparing myself for it in any way and I don't have any feelings about it."

City, who won the Premier League three times between 2009 and 2018, have denied all of the charges and are set to lodge an appeal against the verdict.

Of his longtime rival and Man City coach Pep Guardiola, Klopp said: "I also know what I said about it in the past and how if there's ever a parade, I'll be there. But it doesn't feel like that anymore. My respect for Pep Guardiola and the football played at City during the time we played against each other, in the way they played back then and how they brought football to life on the pitch -- plus what an opponent they proved to be for us at the very highest level -- is far too great for me to be able to say anything now."

Klopp was also tight-lipped on Germany's captain for the Nations League tie -- his third match in charge of the national team. The new Germany coach has a completely new squad to work with after he selected two groups for the four fixtures during this international window.

With regular captain Joshua Kimmich allowed to leave the camp after he featured in a 1-1 draw in the Netherlands and the shock home loss to Greece, Klopp must decide who wears the armband for this clash in Munich.

"The team will be led onto the pitch tomorrow by the player with the most international caps," Klopp said on Wednesday.

Captain question aside, Klopp did hint that Bayern Munich goalkeeper Jonas Urbig would play at his home stadium of Allianz Arena.

"Feel free to ask 'who might be a captaincy option,' but I don't reveal the starting lineup now. You can look them up yourselves," said Klopp. "I can only say that Jonas Urbig won't wear the armband in his first international match."

Urbig took part in a news conference after Klopp and expressed his delight at making his Germany debut.

"It's a moment you've worked towards your whole life and I'm simply delighted to have the opportunity tomorrow to play here in our own stadium and do my part to help us as a team achieve our first victory," Urbig said. "This No. 1 topic isn't something I'm concerned with. My focus is really on reaching my limit every day and pushing it even further. And everything else will perhaps fall into place over time."

Germany are without a win in four fixtures after a World Cup last-32 exit to Paraguay followed a group-stage loss to Ecuador, but Serbia are on an equally poor run.

Serbia have lost both Nations League fixtures by a 2-1 score to the Netherlands and Greece, respectively, after they suffered heavy defeats to Cape Verde and Mexico during the summer.

"Serbia's approach won't be much different from what Greece did. What makes Serbia particularly difficult to play against is their experience," Klopp said. "They also have some excellent footballers. They know all the tricks of the trade, so we have to be prepared for that.

"It's not the best period in Serbian football at the moment, but the players themselves know what's at stake. An opponent that sits deep is a major challenge for any team, at any stage of development."

Following the game against Serbia on Thursday, Germany will close out Nations League play for the September/October international window with a second match against Greece, this time in Thessaloniki on Oct. 4.

stories.summary: Alex Ovechkin holds the record for the most individual career goals in NHL history. Which other players are at the top of the list?
stories.body:

"The Great One" finished his illustrious 20-year career with an NHL-record 894 goals in 1,487 games. It is a mark that stood until Alex Ovechkin broke it in April 2025.

stories.headline: NBA preseason buzz: Latest on trades, news and intel
stories.summary: The NBA regular season is less than a month away, and we're tracking all the news, deals, and trades across the league.
stories.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Sept. 22 as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 30

Nuggets add Nembhard on two-way deal

Guard Ryan Nembhard has agreed to a two-way contract with the Denver Nuggets, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Nembhard, 23, played 60 games (27 starts) for the Dallas Mavericks in 2025-26 after signing as an undrafted free agent. He was traded to the Atlanta Hawks then to the Charlotte Hornets this offseason before being waived.

Sept. 29

Charania: NBA reviewing finalists' bids for Vegas team

ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the NBA is currently reviewing finalist bids for a new expansion team in Las Vegas. The price range is currently speculated at $12-13 billion with a new arena factored into the cost.

The three final groups are Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo, sources told ESPN.

Will KAT take a pay cut in next Knicks deal?

On "NBA Today," ESPN's Malika Andrews detailed Karl-Anthony Towns' mindset toward contract negotiations with the defending champion New York Knicks.

"Towns, from what I have been told, is willing -- similarly to what Jalen Brunson did [but the] numbers aren't the same -- to take a pay cut," Andrews said. "But the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable."

Towns, 30, is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension through June 30.

Embiid "full participant" in first Sixers' practice
Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday.

"He looked great," Nurse said of Embiid. "Very, very good news from the standpoint of where it's been the last couple years, last couple summers leading into today. ... It's great to see."

After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries.

He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain.

The only Sixers player who did not participate in Tuesday's practice according to a team spokesperson was backup big man Adem Bona, who is dealing with a sprained left foot.

Anfernee Simons, who signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract to join Philadelphia in July, said Embiid's presence in the gym was already notable leading up to the start of camp.

"Everybody's been impressed around here about how he's come in and worked," Simons said. "Joel is going to be Joel. He's going to be a dominant player always. We just want to continue for him to be himself, as well, and I think everybody's going to be able to work around that."

Despite the injuries, the 10-year veteran still averaged 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game last season.

Embiid's inclusion only added to what several Sixers players described as an "exciting" opening day with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown completing their first official practice with the franchise.

"With any team, we got to start somewhere, and then we got to get better and better, and just keep trying to reach our ceiling, right?" Nurse said. "That happens day-to-day. Can we get up tomorrow, like, 98% as excited as we did today? It's going to be hard to get as excited as we all were today, right?

"But we need to come back, and we need to keep climbing that mountain. That's a daily process. I just want them to reach their potential. If they do, great things are going to happen." -- Dave McMenamin

Hoop Collective: The 2026 NBA Media Day reaction special

Brian Windhorst is joined by ESPN reporters from around the league to check in on Monday's Media Days. Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vince Goodwill, Jamal Collier, Anthony Slater and Michael C. Wright all hop on the podcast to discuss the biggest storylines throughout the NBA ahead of training camp.

Goodwill on the latest between the Knicks and Karl-Anthony Towns: "It wasn't so much what he said, like this full-throated defense of himself, but he said, 'I would like to get my contract done.'

"He said, 'I would like to stay in New York for the rest of my career.' And then he kind of ended it and because of the way the Knicks operated, it wasn't like you had space for a follow-up.

"And then someone else, I think Ian Begley asked him, 'Are you OK with playing this out through the season or do you want to table contract talks?' and he basically said, 'Everybody's going to be a little uncomfortable around here.'"
